page.$description: White flat fallback; the light page gradient retains its 115deg angle and 0%, 45%, 100% stops, all white

input.$description: Control boundary, SC 1.4.11: 3.62:1 on white. slate.300 measured 1.52:1

tertiary.$description: Smallest body colour: 5.87:1 on white, 4.64:1 on frost.200, the dark end of the page gradient

placeholder.$description: Input placeholder, slate.600: 5.87:1 on white and 5.22:1 on the muted field, so the hint clears 4.5:1 like running text. Every field still carries a visible label above it (COMPONENTS.md, Text field); slate.500 stays forbidden as text

elevated.$description: Menus, popovers, dialogs and the command palette: the surface that sits above the page. In dark and black it is lighter than surface, because a shadow alone does not read on a dark ground

scrim.$description: Translucent overlay behind a dialog or a mobile drawer. Decorative: it dims, it never carries meaning on its own

border-input.$description: The boundary of a control the user has to find (field, checkbox, select): 3:1 on surface, sunken, muted and elevated, unlike the decorative border roles

placeholder.$description: Input placeholder. Held to 4.5:1 like running text on surface, sunken, muted and elevated, so a hint is readable even though every field also carries a visible label

disabled.$description: Fill of a disabled control. Neutral, never the action colour, so the inactive state reads without relying on opacity

on-disabled.$description: Label of a disabled control on the disabled fill: 4.5:1, legible while unmistakably inactive (the fill, not a faded label, carries the state)

elevation.$description: Elevation, four levels and level 0 (DESIGN_HANDOFF A10). Level 0 is no shadow: a flat surface on the page, Tailwind's own `shadow-none`, which needs no token. A level is chosen by the kind of surface, not by its z layer (A12): a toast sits above a dialog yet casts level 2. Each level has one geometry, drawn in the shadow colour of the theme it is in, and is emitted as `--elevation-<level>` inside each `[data-theme]` block and as the preset's `shadow-<level>`, a `var()`, so a `shadow-c-*` colour or an opacity modifier does not apply to it. In dark and black a shadow alone does not separate a layer from its ground, so menus and dialogs pair their level with the `elevated` surface.

raised.$description: Level 1, a resting card or a raised control on the page: the `shadow.card` geometry, in this theme's lighter shadow colour (`shadow-1`).

overlay.$description: Level 2, a dropdown, menu, popover, select list, tooltip or toast over the page: the `shadow.pop` geometry, in this theme's heavier shadow colour (`shadow-2`).

drawer.$description: Level 3, a drawer or sheet fixed to a screen edge. No offset, so the shadow falls on the open edge whichever edge the panel is on. Heavier shadow colour.

dialog.$description: Level 4, a modal dialog over the scrim, the strongest shadow. Heavier shadow colour.

selection-ring-width.$description: Width of the existing selected-control ring; separate from keyboard focus.

breakpoint.$description: Breakpoints, mobile-first: each step is a min-width, and a screen is designed at its narrowest first. 360 px is the smallest device designed for; every screen still reflows without horizontal scroll at 320 CSS px (WCAG 1.4.10). In rem, Tailwind 4's own default steps, so a media query scales with the reader's default font size and a consumer that takes the preset's `screens` sees no change; the px figures in each description hold at a 16 px root.

sm.$description: 640 px. A large phone held sideways, a small tablet.

md.$description: 768 px. Tablet portrait. A width step only: a product's own narrow layout may also depend on height or pointer, and is its own query.

lg.$description: 1024 px. Laptop; a secondary column can move beside the content.
